correctness.finding: PASS. For distinct odd primes r_i!=5, Carmichael primitive divisors q_i of F_{25r_i} have rank of apparition 25r_i and are pairwise distinct from 2 and 5. The parity-steered multiplier U_R makes v_{q_i}(F_{25U_RQ}) odd for every admissible prime Q by the standard Fibonacci valuation formula; v_5(F_n)=3 is also odd. Thus the squarefree kernel contains at least 5,q_1,...,q_R, and the fundamental discriminant contains at least R+1 distinct odd prime divisors. Gauss genus theory then gives 2-rank at least R, while Kishi's theorem contributes the independent factor 5. The infinitude argument is also valid: finiteness of the quadratic fields would force a fixed squarefree kernel D along infinitely many Q, hence infinitely many integral points (A_Q,L_{mQ}) on the fixed nonsingular quartic Y^2=5D^2X^4-4, contradicting Siegel. I independently checked the submitted example primes: 230686501 divides F_75 with no earlier divisor-index among divisors of 75, and 701 divides F_175 with no earlier divisor-index among divisors of 175.

originality.finding: PASS, with an explicit access residual. Kishi's 2008 abstract states universal divisibility by 5 for Q(sqrt(-F_{50s+25})) and construction of an unramified cyclic quintic extension; it does not advertise unbounded 2-rank. Chakraborty--Rao--Dabhole's 2026 work uses the same family and genus-theoretic/Fibonacci valuation ingredients to obtain an additional factor of 2 on a restricted family, not arbitrarily many independent 2-torsion directions. Targeted searches for unbounded 2-rank or arbitrary powers of 2 within Kishi's Fibonacci family found no covering result. The 2008 Kishi full text was unavailable through open sources; authorized institutional retrieval was attempted and stopped at human verification, so no inaccessible content is claimed as read.

scientific_value.finding: PASS. Unbounded 2-rank inside one fixed Fibonacci-parametrized class-number-five family is a substantial strengthening of a single additional factor of 2: it forces class numbers divisible by 5*2^R for every prescribed R and proves infinitely many distinct fields at each rank level. The theorem does not overclaim density or the full 2-primary class-group structure.
